plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare branches become wreathed in spicy, clove-scented blossoms before a single leaf appears. The flowers, borne singly or in pairs, glow in shades of pink and white against the cold late-winter sky.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter, February to March in temperate climates (earlier in milder ones)
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the Midwestern United States, such as St. Louis, Missouri, and its native southern China
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are treasured across East Asia as a symbol of perseverance, because they open in the cold while other plants are still dormant.

plants.name: Cercis occidentalis
plants.description: A small, multi-stemmed native tree that bursts into clouds of magenta-pink, pea-like flowers along bare twigs. Heart-shaped leaves follow once the show fades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, roughly February to April
plants.location: Foothills and canyons of California, USA
plants.funFact: Western redbud is a legume, and its flowers grow straight out of the bark of branches and trunks. Many California Native peoples have long used its flexible shoots in basketry.

plants.name: Nerine sarniensis
plants.description: Glittering, wavy-petaled blooms in fiery scarlet and orange appear in clusters on bare stalks, with petals that seem dusted with tiny crystals. They shine out of autumn fynbos on rocky Cape slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere autumn, March to April
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa (including the Cape Town area)
plants.funFact: Despite the name 'Guernsey lily', this bulb is native to South Africa. It became popular in Europe after bulbs washed ashore or were shipped from the Cape in the 1600s.
